claim: Mouse hippocampal astrocytes activated by neuron-released endocannabinoids modulate putative single CA3-CA1 hippocampal synapses.
source: Here we show that mouse hippocampal astrocytes activated by endogenous (neuron-released endocannabinoids or GABA) or exogenous (single astrocyte Ca2+ uncaging) stimuli modulate putative single CA3-CA1 hippocampal synapses.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly, and the manuscript presents experimental data supporting this claim throughout the Results section.

claim: Mouse hippocampal astrocytes activated by GABA modulate putative single CA3-CA1 hippocampal synapses.
source: Here we show that mouse hippocampal astrocytes activated by endogenous (neuron-released endocannabinoids or GABA) or exogenous (single astrocyte Ca2+ uncaging) stimuli modulate putative single CA3-CA1 hippocampal synapses.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly, and experimental data in Figure 3 and related text demonstrate GABA-mediated astrocyte activation and synaptic modulation.

claim: Mouse hippocampal astrocytes activated by single astrocyte Ca2+ uncaging modulate putative single CA3-CA1 hippocampal synapses.
source: Here we show that mouse hippocampal astrocytes activated by endogenous (neuron-released endocannabinoids or GABA) or exogenous (single astrocyte Ca2+ uncaging) stimuli modulate putative single CA3-CA1 hippocampal synapses.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly, and Figure 5 presents experimental data showing Ca2+ uncaging in single astrocytes induces synaptic modulation.

claim: The astrocyte-mediated synaptic modulation is biphasic and consists of an initial glutamate-mediated potentiation followed by a purinergic-mediated depression of neurotransmitter release.
source: The astrocyte-mediated synaptic modulation was biphasic and consisted of an initial glutamate-mediated potentiation followed by a purinergic-mediated depression of neurotransmitter release.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data in Figures 2-6 showing the biphasic response and pharmacological dissection of the two components.

claim: The temporal dynamic properties of the biphasic synaptic regulation depend on the firing frequency of neuronal activity that stimulated astrocytes.
source: The temporal dynamic properties of this biphasic synaptic regulation depended on the firing frequency and duration of the neuronal activity that stimulated astrocytes.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, and Figure 6 presents experimental data showing how different firing frequencies affect the temporal properties of the biphasic synaptic regulation.

claim: The temporal dynamic properties of the biphasic synaptic regulation depend on the duration of neuronal activity that stimulated astrocytes.
source: The temporal dynamic properties of this biphasic synaptic regulation depended on the firing frequency and duration of the neuronal activity that stimulated astrocytes.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, and Figure 6 presents experimental data showing how different durations of neuronal activity affect the temporal properties of the biphasic synaptic regulation.

claim: Single astrocytes can decode neuronal activity and release distinct gliotransmitters to differentially regulate neurotransmission at putative single synapses.
source: Present results indicate that single astrocytes can decode neuronal activity and, in response, release distinct gliotransmitters to differentially regulate neurotransmission at putative single synapses.
evidence: The abstract concludes with this interpretation, which is supported by the experimental data throughout the manuscript showing that single astrocytes release both glutamate and ATP/adenosine in response to different patterns of neuronal activity.
